chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillah, from al-Sindī ibn Muḥammad al-Bazzāz, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who sees blood for five days and purity for five days, then sees blood for four days and sees purity for six days,

So he said: “If she sees blood, she does not perform salat; and if she sees purity, she performs salat during the period up to thirty days. Then when the thirty days are complete, and she sees flowing blood, she performs ghusl, binds herself, and stuffs herself with cotton at the time of every salat. And if she sees yellowish discharge, she performs wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.اسْتَثْفَرَتْ: she fastens or binds cloth for protection from bleeding
key_terms.الدَّمَ: menstrual or vaginal blood discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: a state of ritual purity in which salat is performed
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ يَوْمًا: the thirty-day period used here as a legal threshold

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who alternates between bleeding and purity in irregular days?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman whose bleeding and periods of purity alternate in an irregular pattern. It explains when she leaves salat, when she resumes it, and what acts of ritual purification she performs after thirty days in the case of continued bleeding.
